title: Tesla + SpaceX? Same shares. Smaller slice?

sources.note: Special committee exploring deeper relationship with SpaceX including possible business combination; no assurance of consummation.

claims.text: Tesla disclosed a special committee exploring a deeper relationship with SpaceX, including a possible business combination.
The filing says there is no assurance that a transaction will be consummated.
Illustration only: 10 shares out of 100 is 10%; if total shares increase to 125 while those 10 are retained, the stake is 8%.
A lower ownership percentage alone does not establish a lower investment value; what is acquired and the price paid matter.

scenes.title: Same shares. Smaller slice?
scenes.narration: Could you keep every share you own, but end up owning less of the company?

scenes.title: Possible does not mean agreed.
scenes.narration: Tesla disclosed a committee exploring a deeper relationship with SpaceX, including a possible combination. Possible. Keep the confetti in the drawer. A deal is not guaranteed.

scenes.title: Ten shares. Ten percent. Then eight.
scenes.narration: Here is an example, not proposed deal terms. You own ten of one hundred shares. Issue twenty-five more, and your ten shares now represent eight percent. Rude.

scenes.title: A smaller slice of what?
scenes.narration: But eight percent does not automatically mean your investment lost value. If new shares buy valuable assets, you own a smaller percentage of a different business.
labels: Ownership percentage is not investment value

scenes.title: Read the terms.
scenes.narration: So ask: what is being bought, at what price, and how does ownership change? Then check the required approvals. A headline cannot answer those questions.

scenes.title: The percentage is only half the story.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: count your slice, but also understand the whole business. That is the part a merger headline leaves out.

character_cast.notes: The existing recurring hybrid character guides the viewer; possible corporate transaction is not personified as an actual event.
